title: Service latency: customer briefing & follow-up templates
summary: Working set of concise, customer-facing messages for multi-step latency incidents. Includes short status-page updates (initial, interim, resolution) and a customer postmortem skeleton suitable for external distribution. Designed for SRE + CS to adapt quickly with incident-specific facts.
status_page_templates: Initial (15–30 min): Investigation in progress: We are currently investigating increased latency affecting {{affected_services}} in {{region}}. Impact: requests are experiencing elevated response times and occasional timeouts. Scope: approximately {{percent}} of requests. What we're doing: engineering is actively investigating root cause and applying mitigations to restore normal latency. We will provide an update within 30 minutes. Incident ID: {{incident_id}}. Contact: support@redwood.ai for short-term workarounds and status subscription.

Interim update (30–90 min): Mitigation underway: We have identified a likely service/component: {{suspected_component}}. We have deployed a targeted mitigation (temporary configuration change / routing adjustment) that has reduced average latency by ~{{improvement_percent}}. Customers may still see elevated latency for long-running requests or in specific regions ({{affected_regions}}). Next steps: deploy permanent fix and continue monitoring. ETA for wider improvement: ~2 hours. Incident ID: {{incident_id}}.

Follow-up update (post-mitigation): Partial resolution achieved: The applied fix ({{mitigation_action}}) has restored normal latency for ~{{percent_resolved}} of traffic. We are continuing a controlled rollout to the remainder of traffic and validating end-to-end. No data loss detected. If you see continued issues after {{time_window}}, please open a support ticket referencing {{incident_id}}.

Resolution (final status page): Incident resolved: On {{resolution_time}} we completed a full rollout of the fix and observed stable latency within our SLA targets. Impact: elevated latency experienced by customers using {{affected_services}} between {{start_time}} and {{end_time}}. Root cause summary: {{one-line-root-cause}}. Remediation: permanent configuration change / code fix deployed. Post-incident actions: retrospective, automated alert tuning, and additional canary checks. We will publish a customer-facing postmortem within 5 business days. Incident ID: {{incident_id}}.

Short customer-facing blurb for banners/notifications: Experiencing slow responses? We're aware of elevated latency for {{service}} and are actively working on a fix. Subscribe to status updates or contact support for impacts to your account.
customer_postmortem_template: Title: Customer postmortem — {{incident_id}} — Elevated latency impacting {{affected_services}}

Executive summary: On {{start_time}} Redwood Inference experienced elevated latency affecting {{scope}} of requests to {{affected_services}}. The incident lasted until {{end_time}}. No customer data was lost. We prioritized reducing user-facing latency while ensuring safe deploys. This note summarizes impact, root cause, remediation, and recommended customer actions.

What happened (impact): Customers in {{regions}} reported increased response times (median latency rose from {{baseline_ms}}ms to {{peak_ms}}ms) and a small number of timeouts for long-running streams. Affected features: text generation, streaming responses, and embeddings for some model variants. Percentage of customers impacted: ~{{percent}}.

Timeline (high level): - {{start_time}}: Automated alerts triggered for elevated P95 latency. - +5m: SRE begins triage; initial hypothesis routing/load. - +18m: Identify correlation with {{component}} during recent change/traffic spike. - +40m: Roll back/config change or apply mitigation, partial improvement observed. - {{resolution_time}}: Full rollout of fix; metrics returned to baseline.

Root cause: The incident was caused by {{root_cause_brief}} (e.g., a combination of kernel-level scheduling changes, a cache eviction bug, and an inefficient fallback path under tail load). The specific trigger was {{trigger_event}}. This exposed a previously unobserved path that amplified latency under the observed traffic pattern.

Remediation and mitigation: Immediate actions taken: emergency rollback / routing adjustment / increase in buffer limits / temporary scale-up of capacity. Permanent fixes deployed: code patch {{pr_number}} to address fallback path; alert rule changes to detect early signs; additional unit/integration tests added. We also added a canary that exercises the specific traffic pattern and an automated rollback if P95 exceeds threshold.

Preventative actions and timeline: - Short term (next 2 weeks): complete additional validations in staging and increase canary population. - Medium term (1–2 months): refactor the fallback path and implement more granular KPIs for early detection. - Long term (3 months): scheduler/kernel-level mitigations and improved capacity planning for burst traffic.

Customer guidance: What you might see & recommended actions: If you are still seeing elevated latency beyond {{time_window}}, please clear local caches and retry. For mission-critical routes, consider temporarily routing traffic to an unaffected region or using model variants that avoid the impacted execution path. Contact your CSM or support@redwood.ai for assistance and prioritized investigation.

Compensation and SLOs: We're evaluating impacts against SLA commitments. If your service experienced material business impact, please open a support case and reference {{incident_id}}; we will follow our SLA credit process. (Legal/Finance: confirm eligibility and calculations before external statement.)
Who to contact: Primary CS lead: {{csm_name}} (email). SRE lead: {{sre_name}}. For urgent escalations open support ticket and include incident id.
Appendix: Links to artifacts and telemetry: - Incident timeline and raw metrics: {{internal_dashboard_link}} - Deploy/PR references: {{pr_link}} - Related tickets: {{jira_links}}
internal_notes: Use short, plain-language lines for status pages — customers want quick clarity (status, scope, ETA).
Legal must review any line that mentions SLA credits or compensation before it goes live.
If we do not have a confirmed root cause within 72 hours, schedule a customer office hour for affected accounts to walk through next steps.
For large customers (dedicated/private), include per-account exposure metrics and reach out via account channel rather than only public status page.
Suggested Slack channels: #inc-{{incident_id}} (ops), #cs-notify (customer success), #legal-escalations (if compensation language used).
Recommended cadence for a major latency incident: Immediate -> 30m -> 2h -> resolution -> 3-day follow-up -> full postmortem within 5 business days.
Template placeholders to replace before publish: {{incident_id}}, {{affected_services}}, {{percent}}, {{start_time}}, {{end_time}}, {{root_cause_brief}}, {{sre_name}}, {{csm_name}}.
